items.title: Who’s Watching the Agents? Security and Oversight for Autonomous AI
items.summary: AI agents no longer just answer questions. They call tools, touch APIs, make decisions and produce more code, plans and text than any team can read line by line. That raises two questions every engineering team has to answer: how do we keep autonomous agents secure, and how do we keep up with reviewing what they produce? This evening covers both sides. Google’s SAIF 2.0 states that agents need well-defined human controllers and that their actions and planning must be observable. We’ll first look at what that framework demands for securing agentic systems, and then at open-source tooling that makes human oversight practical, even when your agents produce far more than you can read. **THIS MEE…

items.summary: Agentic engineering is building software by directing AI coding agents rather than writing the code yourself. The engineering part comes from how you direct the agents - the goal, the rules, the checks, the coding standards, the tests, the code reviews etc. It speeds things up a lot as Agents are incredibly quick at producing code, much faster than humans, and it allows you much more flexibility in what you build, as you are not just limited to your own knowledge, language or domain expertise. The more time consuming part now, is not the writing code, but the verifying, the testing, the workflow you use to ensure code quality and goal adherence.
